26 The diagram shows a stationary wave on a string. The stationary wave has three nodes N1, N2
and N3.
N1
N2
N3
Which statement is correct?
A
All points on the string vibrate in phase.
B
All points on the string vibrate with the same amplitude.
C
Points equidistant from N2 vibrate with the same frequency and in phase.
D
Points equidistant from N2 vibrate with the same frequency and the same amplitude.

hints: Look at the two loops N1 to N2 and N2 to N3 and recall where the nodes and antinodes are in this stationary wave.
Compare motion on opposite sides of N2: points in the same loop reach maximum displacement together, while points in adjacent loops move in opposite directions.
Think how vibration amplitude depends on distance from the nearest node, so two points the same distance from N2 have the same size of vibration even if they are in different loops.
walkthrough: Identify the pattern: N1, N2 and N3 are nodes, so N1 to N2 is one loop and N2 to N3 is a second loop of the same stationary wave.
State the frequency rule: every point on a stationary wave vibrates with the same frequency, equal to the frequency of the two interfering progressive waves.
State the amplitude rule: amplitude is zero at each node and increases to a maximum at the centre of each loop, depending only on distance from the node.
State the phase rule: all points within one loop are in phase with each other, but points in adjacent loops separated by a node are in antiphase.

Apply to points equidistant from N2 on opposite sides: they have the same frequency and, because the envelope is symmetric, the same amplitude, but they are in opposite loops so they are in antiphase. This is option D.

A.explanation: Points in the N1 to N2 loop move opposite to points in the N2 to N3 loop, so adjacent loops are in antiphase, not all in phase.

B.explanation: Amplitude is zero at N1, N2 and N3 and maximum at each antinode, so amplitude varies with position.

C.explanation: Frequency is the same everywhere, but points on opposite sides of N2 lie in different loops and vibrate in antiphase.

D.explanation: All points share the stationary wave frequency and the amplitude envelope is symmetric about N2, so equal distances from N2 give equal amplitudes.
